Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: perf benchmark scope and timing

Sarah —

Thanks for the clear summary and the logs. I've drafted a minimal reproducibility playbook and MAP milestones attached (acme_map_perf_plan.xlsx). Key points / proposed approach:

1) Goals & acceptance criteria
- Primary metrics: TTFT (time to first token), p50/p95/p99 generation latency, tokens/sec, and error rate.
- Acceptance target: TTFT p50 <= 250ms and p95 <= 800ms for the short-chat template at 50 concurrent clients (cold vs warm baseline to be agreed).

2) Methodology parity (critical)
- Agree on exact model artifact (model name + commit hash), tokenizer version, sequence length distribution, and prompt normalization.
- Use the same load generator (we recommend RedwoodBench v2.1; if you prefer Locust we'll run parity tests with identical traffic shapes).
- Define warm-cache: 1000 prefix requests over 30 minutes vs cold: zero cache.

3) Repro playbook (high level)
- Step A: customer runs local capture with their current harness and shares a short sample (we received your log).
- Step B: Redwood runs instrumented test in a controlled Dedicated pool with identical model and tokenizer.
- Step C: both exchange raw traces and token-level timings; if discrepancy > 20% we do a paired run with per-request detailed tracing.

4) Triage checklist (common discrepancy causes)
- Tokenization mismatch (different tokenizer version or pre/post processing).
- Differences in streaming/chunking: client-side buffering vs server stream flush frequency.
- Batching and KV-cache warmup behavior.
- Quantization/precision mismatch on compared variants.

5) Timeline (proposed)
- Nov 19: agree playbook and provide sample prompt set.
- Nov 20–21: Redwood instrumented runs + one parity run with your harness.
- Nov 22: joint results review and discrepancy triage.
- Nov 30: target for MAP sign if acceptance criteria met; else extend to Dec 14 for additional runs.

I attached the MAP workbook with explicit owners and a draft DocuSign link to the MAP terms. If that timeline works we can schedule the parity run Tuesday morning our time.

Attachment: acme_map_perf_plan.xlsx (Spreadsheet)

Thanks — I'll coordinate with Neha and Karthik on the runbook.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Marcus / Sarah —

Quick technical additions from the bench team (I'm owning the repro):

- Exact run commands we'll use (RedwoodBench v2.1):
  rdbench run --model redwood-7b-v1 --tokenizer v1.2 --concurrency 50 --seq-dist short-chat.json --warmup 1000 --streams 200 --out run_20261119.json

- We'll export token timestamps and KV cache hit/miss stats. Please share a sample of your short-chat prompt set (10–20 prompts) and the sequence-length histogram; that will help reproduce distribution-sensitive batching effects.

- Known gotchas to check:
  * Prompt normalization (trim vs pad) can shift TTFT when the load generator pre-warms differently.
  * If tests compare hosted vs on-prem, ensure equivalent model quantization; a 4-bit vs 8-bit mismatch can impact latency non-linearly.
  * Client-side backpressure: some load generators accumulate tokens before reporting TTFT — we'll include raw socket timestamps to avoid that ambiguity.

I've uploaded a small CSV snapshot of our baseline to the drive link Marcus shared and attached a short metrics extract for context.

Attachment: acme_initial_metrics.csv (CSV)

I'll kick off the instrumented run tomorrow morning and share results by EOD Nov 20.

—Karthik
Bench Lead, Redwood Inference
